Prompting LTX-2
widgets_values:
## LTX-2 Prompting Tips
1. **Core Actions**: Describe events and actions as they occur over time  
2. **Audio**: Describe sounds and dialogue needed for the scene  
3. **Reference Image**: Do not repeat details already present  
4. **Consistency**: Avoid instructions that do not match the reference image, as this will degrade results

nodes.title: User Made Loras
widgets_values: If using some user made LTX-2 loras they sometimes are not trained on audio, so it will produce very noisy audio outputs. Try use KJNodes LTX-2 Lora Loader Advanced in such cases, and set the non video strenght to zero

nodes.title: About Size
widgets_values:
Width & height settings must be divisible by 32 + 1. 
Frame count must be divisible by 8 + 1. 


Running with invalid parameters **will not cause errors**. Instead, the flow will silently choose the closest valid parameters. 

By default, we are using 720p resolution. You can try 1920*1088 if you have a powerful GPU.

nodes.title: Frames formula now automated
widgets_values:
Time Master calculates total frames as:

`ceil(seconds × FPS / 8) × 8 + 1`

This keeps `(frames - 1)` divisible by 8 for LTX.

The four guide-image start frames are then calculated from the segment lengths: 0, seg1, seg1+seg2, seg1+seg2+seg3.

nodes.title: Custom Audio
widgets_values:
**AUDIO START FROM:** 
 For a longer music video, you can create multiple renders in a row. And use the "Trim Audio" node **start index** to set where you want to continue from. For example if the first render was 50 seconds, you can set start index to 50 seconds, and continue render the song from there

----

Mel-band RoFormer is optional for extracting a clean vocal only audio for the sampler. This can be useful for example if its a close up of a singer. For other music where you want instrument and dance to follow the beat, use full music track and not vocals only

https://huggingface.co/Kijai/MelBandRoFormer_comfy/tree/main

nodes.title: Timeline Editor
widgets_values:
**MAX FRAMES** 

Match that to the frames you set for LTX to generate.  (in this workflow its automatic from the "Frames" input node)

**SEGMENTS**  

Add segments and distribute them to your  total frame count. The segments can be adjusted by dragging the border of the visuals. 

Click each segment to enter a segment prompt for that segment

nodes.title: Story tips
widgets_values:
If two sequential images are **very alike** the model might treat it as one continuous scene (and that can be nice sometimes). 

If you want to transition to a new scene, having a different image is often enough. But you can also write at **end of previous prompt** that there is a scene cut. For example write " *At the end, scene cut to a new scene.* ". 


 _ _ _ _   


To create input images from different scenes with consistent characters you can use Qwen Image Edit with Next-Scene and/or Multiple-Angles lora. 

Flux Klein is also able to change reference image characters to a new scene while keeping their identity. 

(or use Googles Nano Banana, Chat GPT, or Qwen Chat to acheive the same)

nodes.title: Video settings
widgets_values:
If low on Ram/Vram, try width height to 832 x 480 or 960 x 544.  If you can, run at 1280 x 720 or higher.


Length in seconds :  try 5, 10 or 20. 
fps : 24 or 25 (or 48 or 50 if your pc can run it)

nodes.title: SEGMENT SYNC - IMPORTANT!
widgets_values:
Segment frames are now calculated automatically from **Safe LTX Frames**.

Default: 30s × 24 FPS → 721 frames → 181 / 180 / 180 / 180.

Important: Prompt Relay receives the new `max_frames`, but its internal Timeline segment lengths are still widget data. If you change seconds/FPS, update the Prompt Relay segment lengths to match the calculated segment values.

nodes.title: PromptRelayEncodeTimeline (old disabled reference)
TIME MASTER - Auto FPS / Seconds / Frames
widgets_values:
Use **FPS MASTER** and **Length (seconds) MASTER**.

Total frames are calculated as `ceil(seconds × FPS / 8) × 8 + 1`.

That total feeds: Prompt Relay `max_frames`, EmptyLTXVLatentVideo `length`, Latent Audio, TrimAudioDuration and the global `frames` variable.

Segments are auto-split into 4 equal parts for image-guide timing: seg1 gets the +1 frame.

A young man with glasses sits at a desk in a cozy creator studio, facing the camera and speaking naturally. He wears a dark blue overshirt over a light T-shirt, with a simple necklace visible. The shot is a centered medium shot, with a camera visible in the foreground and a microphone on a boom arm near him. His hands are placed together on the desk at first, and he maintains calm eye contact with the lens while speaking in a steady and confident way. The background is rich and detailed, with shelves, lenses, plants, warm lamps, and blue ambient lighting.

The camera cuts to a tighter medium close-up. The young man continues speaking directly to the camera with a focused and engaged expression. He raises both hands naturally in front of his chest while explaining, using open-palmed gestures and small finger movements to emphasize his points. The microphone remains visible beside him, and the softly blurred studio background shows warm practical lights, shelves, and camera equipment. His head moves slightly as he talks, and the overall performance feels natural and presenter-like.

The shot changes to a three-quarter side angle medium shot. The young man keeps speaking while turning slightly toward the side, as if continuing a longer explanation. He lifts one hand in a presenting gesture while the other hand stays closer to the desk, creating a natural conversational rhythm. The microphone on the boom arm is prominent in the frame. The studio environment feels layered and professional, with bookshelves, plants, decorative lighting, a monitor, and camera gear in the background. His expression is thoughtful, focused, and animated.

The video returns to a centered medium shot of the young man at the desk. He continues speaking in a calmer, more settled way, gradually bringing his hands back together on the tabletop. He looks directly into the camera with a composed and confident expression, ending with a slight natural smile. The camera in the foreground, the microphone, the plants, and the warm-and-blue studio lighting all remain visible, reinforcing the creator studio atmosphere. The shot feels like the closing part of a talking-head presentation.
